thread:
Sam H: quick question — who should own the decision to fallback during a canary: the rollout controller (central) or the runtime on each host (local)?
Lucy P: my vote is hybrid — controller for policy + slow signals, runtime for fast emergency cuts
Anita R: ^this. central policy defines when to ramp up/down but runtime needs a fast local firebreak (OOM, hard timeouts)
Mike L: latency-wise local wins. controller-to-runtime RTT is too high for a 100ms SLA
Kevin Z: agree with Lucy/Anita, but need a clear rpc contract so runtime can ask for "policy advice" when borderline
Sam H: what signals do we need in that contract? p50/p95 latency, error rate, model quality? any others?
Lucy P: add request skew (per-route), cache hit rate, inference queue depth
Anita R: also token-drop counts, kv-cache thrash rate, and model loading churn
Mike L: if we make the local decision we risk inconsistency across hosts — need deterministic fallback reasons encoded
Kevin Z: proposal: controller publishes policy with thresholds + probe window size; runtime keeps local short-window metrics and a small rule-engine. if local metric > threshold -> local fallback and emit event
Sam H: can we avoid controller churn? controllers often churn during deploys which makes policy unstable
Lucy P: controllers should version policies. rollout attaches policy_version to traffic lease so rollbacks are atomic
Anita R: +1. policy_version in the handoff avoids races. runtime reconciles desired policy_version periodically
Mike L: how does telemetry get back to controller? we shouldn't overload central with raw traces
Kevin Z: runtime emits compact signals: {policy_version, route, window_ms, p95, err_rate, decisions} as compressed protobufs to kafka
Sam H: sounds good. what about quality signals (semantic regressions)? evaluator can be slow
Lucy P: evaluator streams anomaly alerts to a topic; controller can mark policy as degraded and trigger slow-rollbacks (not emergency local)
Anita R: separate channels: fast control (local decisions, health) and slow control (quality/eval). local fast path ignores slow quality unless controller flips global flag
Mike L: we need a clear fallback taxonomy: soft-fallback (gradual reroute), hard-fallback (immediate switch), degraded-mode (rate-limited) — each has different ops impact
Kevin Z: implement enums in the contract: SOFT | HARD | DEGRADED and a TTL for local enforcement
Sam H: what about single-request atomicity? can't have some requests partially routed during handoff
Lucy P: use a short-lived traffic lease token. when runtime receives a new model version it drains active sessions, then exchanges lease token with controller
Anita R: add a handshake step: runtime -> controller: PREPARE(model_id, capacity_hint) controller -> runtime: APPROVE(policy_version, lease_ttl) runtime -> controller: ACK
Mike L: sample handshake snippet for logs:
```
PREPARE model=x1 v=2026-03-21T12:00Z cap=32
APPROVE policy=v17 ttl=30s
ACK
```
Kevin Z: ops will want observability: produce decision events with reason codes, metrics pre/post fallback, and sample request ids for replay
Sam H: do we allow runtime to escalate to fallback without controller when controller unreachable?
Lucy P: yes, if controller is unreachable for >3s and local health is bad -> local HARD fallback; then emit event and reconcile later
Anita R: but require signed policy_version so we don't introduce rogue fallbacks after controller comes back — runtime should validate last-known policy sig
Mike L: security: use mutual TLS for controller<->runtime comms, sign policy blobs, and rotate keys via KMS
Kevin Z: one more: how to test this? recommend chaos tests: controller flapping, network partition, delayed telemetry, and synthetic model regressions
Sam H: action items: Anita to draft RPC contract (probe + handshake + decision events), Lucy to design policy_version lifecycle, Mike to add local rule-engine POC, Kevin to sketch telemetry compact schema
Anita R: on it — will put RFC draft in /docs and ping this thread when ready :thumbsup:
